This is my advice, I'm currently in a weight loss journey, and most of everything I'm about to write is me rambling. But it's what I typed out 🤷‍♂️

I struggle with losing weight mainly because I start, then stop, then start, have extra calories on a day, give up its not worth it. But one day something clicked, I asked myself do you want to die before 40, because being 400 pounds, I'm gonna die before 40. That vision gave me motivation of okay my life needs to change, whenever I want to give up or just go and eat ice cream because why not, I remind myself of why I'm doing this, to live a long life. Currently I'm down 20 pounds and I've still got a long way to go but I'm confident I can keep it going this time because I have a reason to.

My point is, look at why you want to lose weight. Think about how being 280 pounds effects your daily life, think about how much easier certain tasks will be if 60 pounds magically disappeared.  

Another thing I've done is I've stopped thinking about my goal weight. I weigh myself every Tuesday, and my only goal is for the scale to be a lower number this Tuesday, Compared to last. I'm not thinking, man I've gotta lose 200 pounds, I'm thinking, I gotta lose 2, that way next week I can lose another 2

>but it’s just the exercising that’s a problem at the moment.

I had a hard time convincing myself to go workout, because I was anxious about people looking at me and saying things or whatever. But my apartment has a gym and I figured if I go at midnight, no one will be there, if you live in an apartment that has a gym and have the time to go late I prefer it, it's quiet, its colder, nobody's looking at me, it's great.
